newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse down, catches up with Friday loss.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse down, catches up with Friday loss.

text.p: German shares started bourse trade down on Monday as floor dealings caught up with losses made during late Friday electronic dealings and weaker German bonds and a lower dollar weighed on the market.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares started 14.87 points, or 0.55 percent, down at 2,668.38.
After the close of floor dealings on Friday, the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index, had fallen as profits were taken on the bond markets.
Dealers said they saw the DAX index making no dramatic moves ahead of the U.S. elections on Tuesday, but said it was also well-supported around current levels.

The morning's main market-moving news was the confirmation of the merger between British Telecommunications Plc and U.S firm MCI Communications. German mixed utility Viag AG, BT's partner in Germany, climbed over one percent, or six marks to 571.50 marks.

Dealers said there was also interest in the auto sector, dominant last week. Apart from Viag, car makers Daimler AG and Volkswagen AG were the only DAX stocks to be in positive territory. VW was up two marks at 612 marks, while Daimler was up 24 pfennigs at 90.65 marks.
